fixes.explanation: Yes, that's the question. God asks, “Is it a time for you yourselves to live in your paneled houses, while this house lies in ruins?” He puts their paneled houses right next to this house lying in ruins. That's the picture He points to, friend.
It's the opposite, friend. God says, “You put on clothes but never get warm.” So they get dressed, and the warmth never comes. They put the clothes on, and they still don't get warm.
That's right. God says, “You put on clothes but never get warm.” They put the clothes on, but they still don't get warm. So False is the answer, baker.

Yes. God says, “Therefore, on account of you the heavens have withheld their dew and the earth has withheld its crops.” The heavens withhold the dew, and the earth withholds its crops. Two things held back at once.

That's the other direction, friend. God says, “I have summoned a drought on the fields and on the mountains…” A drought is a dry stretch, and a flood is the opposite. The dew being withheld in verse 10 fits the dry picture.
Not quite, friend. God says the drought is “…on man and beast, and on all the labor of your hands.” So beasts are named right alongside people. The drought doesn't spare them.
That's right, friend. God says He has summoned the drought “…on man and beast, and on all the labor of your hands.” The animals are named in it, not skipped over. So the drought doesn't spare them.
